claim: A taxpayer appeals an assessment by filing Form 130 with the assessing official; deadline is June 15 of the assessment year if the Form 11 notice was mailed before May 1, otherwise June 15 of the year the tax bill is mailed.
After a Form 130 filing, the assessing official schedules a preliminary informal meeting, then reports to the county PTABOA, which must hold a hearing within 180 days of filing.
If unsatisfied with the PTABOA decision, or if PTABOA fails to rule within 180 days, the taxpayer may appeal to the Indiana Board of Tax Review with Form 131.

The last assessment is presumed correct, but the assessor bears the burden of proof if the assessment rose more than 5% over the prior assessment date (exceptions for new improvements/renovations/zoning/use changes).
Assessed value is meant to reflect the price that would induce the owner to sell and a buyer to purchase, reflecting current use.

For assessment dates after Dec 31, 2024, the homestead standard deduction is $48,000 in 2025, $40,000 in 2026, $30,000 in 2027, $20,000 in 2028 (text continues for later years).
For assessment dates before Jan 1, 2025 the deduction was the lesser of 60% of assessed value or $48,000.

To get a new homestead deduction a taxpayer applies to the county auditor; applications filed before the annual deadline apply to the next tax bill (example given: complete by Jan 15, 2026 for 2025 pay 2026).
A supplemental homestead deduction (IC 6-1.1-12-37.5) is automatic for those receiving the standard deduction; percentage phases up to 66.7% by taxes payable 2031.

Indiana mortgage foreclosure is judicial: the mortgagee proceeds in circuit, superior or probate court of the county where the property lies.
In a foreclosure of a mortgage, process for execution of judgment may not issue for three months after the complaint is filed (12 months for mortgages executed before Jan 1, 1958).

Owner-occupied residential foreclosures require a presuit notice; the court sends notice of the right to a settlement conference, which the debtor must request within 30 days of service of the complaint.
Judgment of foreclosure requires, among other conditions, that at least 60 days have elapsed since the presuit notice was sent.
If the defendant pays principal and interest due with costs before final judgment, the foreclosure proceeding is dismissed per section 11; payment after judgment stays the proceedings.
Court gives personal judgment against parties liable on the debt; balance after sale may be levied on other property where an express agreement for payment exists.
